I'm under the assumption that all of this automation is an opportunity for more economic independence. There will be more creativity and customization put into each product. Instead of filling out a job application, you offer services to the public. Employment might be more collaborative than hierarchical.

You can already see it starting to develop with the Sharing Economy with stuff like airbnb, lyft, etsy and craigslist. There is a boom of craft brewers and distillers. This is only the beginning. I believe it'll get more radical, as automation becomes more radical.

I personally believe the best thing we can do is to drop petty regulations that stand in the way for the purpose of employing middle men.

Anyways please share you ideas.

I also like the idea behind popup events. There could be a planner, a host, a promoter, a caterer, a bar tender and possibly performers that set up events every weekend.

I actually think automated construction might be a wash, because more projects would be on the table. More people might want to build additions on their homes if it's as simple and cheap as only dealing with one or two contractors with a machine that does all the work.

Fixed my 70yo neighbour's wifi.

It's very easy to me, but to her it was magic and numerology. There's always one small technical thing to do whenever you touch anything.

Installing the driver required navigating some menus, since it was one install disc for a bunch of different products. It didn't have the ability to recognize the dongle automatically.

I had to try several routers before hitting on the correct one, because there was no way to know which one was hers. The name had been changed from the default one years ago. Also why does the key have to be case-sensitive?

In the end, I switched the dongle from front to back, since the previous one had been kicked and that killed it, and it suddenly tried to connect to another wifi router. Took me less than ten seconds to fix, but she'd be at a loss for days.

Why is do they make it so hard? It's like they want people to be miserable. These are consumer products, not everyone has an IT department to come in and know all the technical details for them.

It's all about security vs. convenience. Striking a balance between easily usable product and making it secure is a hard task and most router manufacturers make their own protocols for default SSIDs and passwords and where those information are stored makes it hard for the average person to decipher it without reading the manual. They want it to be easy to use but not easy for other people to just break into it.

why does the key have to be case-sensitive?

It's to increase the number of possible characters for a given password. For default passwords, it's better to avoid characters that have similar appearance with its upper and lower case counterpart, and with numbers to boot.

Why is do they make it so hard? It's like they want people to be miserable. These are consumer products, not everyone has an IT department to come in and know all the technical details for them.

A consumer grade wireless router is a set and forget device. Most people won't notice it doing its job unless it breaks or have some mis-configuration (after a reset by a user, power outage, bad flash, etc). As a result, the owner of that device won't readily know what to do to fix it. The basics of the technology used by a router is also harder to comprehend if you're crash coursing it (after your router failed or similar) and with numerous mis-information about troubleshooting it on the Internet, it adds up.

Maybe, just maybe the case sensitiveness adds a relevant amount of security. All the rest though? That's just plain indifference.

Not to mention that the OS isn't that helpful either. I know what all the possible errors are, but the OS is no help telling me which ones it might be, and definitely does not help in telling me how to fix things. I had to bring all that knowledge myself.

Just making it try a different key is not immediately obvious, either, come to think of it. It stupidly keeps trying to use the same wrong key unless you go into the settings to change it. Again, I know this, but your average granny doesn't.

I just hate how there's this basic unwillingness to make it easy, because someone with the technical skills doesn't even consciously remember half the problems that are fixed in a few seconds.

There are just so many places in which the process can fail because of a minor issue, it's just plain unfair. In five minutes I saw so many things that would have thrown my neighbour off, I don't blame her for being scared of misconfiguring something and then it stops working.
